children: Ather Energy shares rose for the fourth consecutive session on Monday, gaining 4 per cent to hit a fresh high of Rs 1,679 after the company launched its new electric scooter, Konarc, in Bengaluru on Saturday.
The stock has gained more than 16 per cent over the past four sessions.
Brokerages have maintained a positive view on the stock following the launch.

Emkay Global Financial Services retained its "buy" rating on Ather Energy and set a target price of Rs 2,200, implying more than 36 per cent upside from Friday's closing level. The brokerage said the stock could double from current levels over the next three to four years.
On the new model, Emkay Global said the Konarc showcases several customer-oriented features and is backed by strong engineering.
Ather Energy launched the Ather Konarc at its annual Community Day on August 29. The electric scooter is priced starting at Rs 99,999, marking the company's entry into the mass-market segment.
Ather CEO and co-founder Tarun Mehta had earlier said the company was preparing to launch its mass-market scooter as India's electric two-wheeler market moves beyond early adopters.

Emkay Global said the production of Konarc will start at Ather's Hosur facility, with deliveries scheduled to begin from September 2026. This will reduce the company's initial dependence on its Aurangabad Industrial City (AURIC) facility, the brokerage said, citing the company.
AURIC is expected to scale up from the December or March quarter, with full ramp-up expected by the first half of FY28. The facility is expected to add 42,000 units per month at full ramp-up.

Ather has also indicated a further capacity expansion of 6,000-10,000 units per month at its Hosur facility, as the plant currently caters to only about 50 per cent of demand, Emkay Global said. The company has also indicated that it will develop multiple new formats based on the EL platform and is likely to unveil a motorcycle platform in FY28.
JM Financial said key takeaways from Ather Community Day included the unveiling of the new EL platform and the launch of the Konarc scooter.

The new EL platform has a longer wheelbase of 1,352 mm compared with 1,285 mm for the Rizta, a 14-inch front wheel compared with 12 inches for the Rizta and 100 mm suspension stroke, along with sequential gear-drive transmission and enhanced braking, the brokerage said.

The Konarc S range comprises four variants with 100 km, 125 km, 161 km and 200 km IDC ranges. Deliveries of the 125 km and 161 km variants are scheduled to begin in September 2026, while the 100 km and 200 km variants are slated for the first and third quarters of calendar year 2027, respectively.
Two Konarc Z variants with 125 km and 161 km ranges are slated for the second quarter of calendar year 2027, JM Financial said.

AURIC remains on track to commence operations in the third quarter of FY27, with full ramp-up expected in the first half of FY28. Ather is also looking to optimise its existing Hosur facility to manufacture above its current capacity of around 35,000 units per month, the brokerage said.

The company also showcased a new Magic Key, connected features and Atherstack 7 upgrades, besides Ather Node for residential charging and improvements in battery longevity and vehicle-health monitoring.
Ather Energy will also be added to the MSCI Small Cap Index.
The stock has been on an upward trend. It has gained more than 32 per cent over the past month and has surged 121 per cent since the beginning of the calendar year.
